title.text: Budapest: Adventure Caving Tour with Guide

pills.summary_html: 🧗 2.5 h climbing & crawling▾
pills.pop_html: How hard it is: You climb walls and crawl through narrow passages in the natural parts of the Pál-völgyi-Mátyás-hegyi system, Hungary's longest cave at about 32 km. No caving experience is needed, but you must be fit enough to climb and crawl for about 2.5 hours.

Kit included: Protective overalls, a helmet and a lamp come with the ticket, as do the cave entry fee and the caving guide. Bring comfortable, breathable clothes and closed-toe shoes; sandals, flip-flops and heels are not allowed. There is a changing room on site.
Group size: Groups are capped at 10 participants. Guides are members of the Hungarian Caving Association. The tour runs in English.

Who can join: Not suitable for children under 8, adults over 55, anyone over 120 kg, pregnant women, or people with back problems, mobility impairments or claustrophobia. The cave stays at 10°C (50°F) all year, so the weather outside does not matter.

best_for.pick_html: for fit adults and kids from 8 who want to actually crawl, squeeze and climb underground, because it is the only real caving option and all the gear is supplied
best_for.skip_html: if you are over 55, claustrophobic, have back problems, or just want to see pretty formations without getting on your knees

items.a: Cave entry fee, caving guide, helmet and lamp, protective overalls.

items.q: How warm or cold is it?

items.a: Most expensive here at €74, about €25 per hour. Strict limits: ages 8–55, max 120 kg, no claustrophobia or back problems. Meeting point at Szépvölgyi út 162 is out in the Buda hills, not central.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

pills.summary_html: 🚶 1.5 km paved route▾
pills.pop_html: The walk: The regular route runs about 1.5 km through the cave under Castle Hill on paved, lit paths. A shorter option starts at Dárda Street; the longer one meets at Trinity Square (Szentháromság tér). Shoes and clothes can get dirty if you lean on the walls or the path is muddy.

What you see: Natural limestone caverns joined to 800-year-old man-made cellars. The guide covers how the labyrinth served as wine cellars, bomb shelters and a medieval prison, plus the geology of Castle Hill.

Families: Children from 3 can join, the lowest age limit on this page. Strollers and baby carriages are not allowed, so bring a carrier for little ones. Not suitable for wheelchair users or people with claustrophobia.

Practical: The cave stays at 12°C (54°F), so bring a warm layer and closed-toe shoes. Groups go up to 25 people. There is no mobile signal underground and video recording is not allowed. Tours start on time and late arrivals miss them.

best_for.pick_html: for families with young kids, first-timers and anyone short on time, because at €17 it is the cheapest cave on the list and starts on Castle Hill next to the other sights
best_for.skip_html: if you want real natural cave formations or a small group; this is a lit cellar-and-cave labyrinth with up to 25 people

items.a: Dárda utca 2, 1014 Budapest (shorter tour); Trinity Square for the longer option.

items.q: How warm or cold is it?

items.a: Groups of up to 25, the largest here. More history and cellars than raw cave formations. No strollers, no video recording.

title.text: Budapest: Szemlő-hegyi & Pál-völgyi Caves Guided Walking Tour

pills.pop_html: What's covered: Entry to both Szemlő-hegyi Cave, known as the underground flower garden of Budapest for its mineral formations, and Pál-völgyi Cave, part of Hungary's longest cave system at about 32 km. You walk about 500 m inside each.

pills.summary_html: 🪜 400+ steps, 7 m ladder▾
pills.pop_html: Effort: Both caves are paved and lit, but you climb more than 400 steps and a 7-metre ladder. You must handle several flights of steep stairs without difficulty; it is not possible for people with limited mobility or wheelchair users.

Highlights: Stalactites, stalagmites and glittering calcite crystals in Pál-völgyi, the Theatre Hall echo chamber, an interactive exhibition and educational trail at Szemlő-hegyi, and a look at the old quarry from one of the hidden exits.

Access: Fast-track entry through a separate entrance, with guides from the Hungarian Caving Association who take you into some sections regular visitors cannot enter. English-speaking guide. Food and drinks are on sale, not included.

best_for.pick_html: for anyone who wants real stalactites and crystal formations without crawling, including kids from 5, because you see two natural caves with an expert caving guide on paved paths
best_for.skip_html: if stairs and a ladder are a problem, or you want the adrenaline of squeezing through passages (book the adventure caving tour)

items.a: Entry to 2 caves, English-speaking expert caving guide.
400+ steps and a 7-metre ladder, not for limited mobility. Meeting point in the Buda hills, a trip out of the centre. At €46 it costs nearly 3x the Buda Castle cave.

title.text: Budapest: The WWII Siege of Buda Castle & Bomb Shelter Tour

pills.summary_html: 💣 Real WWII bomb shelter▾
pills.pop_html: What you visit: The cellar of an old dwelling house at the De la Motte–Beer Palace and an authentic Second World War bomb shelter inside the Buda Castle Cave. About 35 minutes of the 90 are spent walking through the cave.

The story: The siege that began on Christmas Eve 1944 when the Soviet Red Army encircled Budapest, told through diaries and memoirs: tens of thousands of soldiers, wounded and civilians sheltering in the castle's caves and cellars, short of water and food, in the cold and the dark.

pills.summary_html: 🗺️ Dísz tér → Trinity Sq.▾
pills.pop_html: Route: Starts at Dísz tér 15 next to the Posta building (look for the turquoise Buda Castle Walks umbrella at the big green gate), continues along Úri Street and Lovas Way, and ends at Szentháromság tér. Part outdoor, part underground, held in all weather.

Who it suits: Recommended from 14. Steep stairs, narrow corridors and sometimes wet surfaces rule out anyone with mobility issues or claustrophobia. The cellar and cave are about 12°C all year, so dress in layers. Starts promptly; latecomers are not waited for.

best_for.pick_html: for history readers and WWII buffs who want the human story behind the tunnels, because it is the only option built around the 1944–45 siege and a real bomb shelter
best_for.skip_html: if you are travelling with kids under 14 or want natural cave formations; the cave section is about 35 minutes of a 90-minute walk

items.a: De la Motte–Beer Palace, Dísz tér 15, 1014 Budapest (green gate next to the Posta building).
Guided tour in English in the Palace District and in the Buda Castle Cave.

title.text: Budapest: Margaret Island 45-Minute Salt Cave Treatment

pills.summary_html: 🧂 Dead Sea salt rocks▾
pills.pop_html: The room: A man-made cave built with salt rocks from the Dead Sea at the Ensana Thermal hotel on Margaret Island. You breathe the salty air during a 45-minute session; the spa pitches it for the respiratory system and stress relief.
Group size: Sessions are limited to 4 participants, the smallest group on this page, so it stays quiet. Noise, phones, cameras, food and drinks are not allowed inside.
Who can join: Not suitable for children under 14, people with claustrophobia, wheelchair users, anyone with a cold, or people over 150 kg.
What to bring: The listing asks you to bring swimwear and flip-flops, as the treatment is run by the Ensana Thermal spa on Margaret Island. Photography and video are not allowed in the cave.

best_for.pick_html: for a rainy-afternoon wind-down or anyone who wants a quiet, low-effort cave experience between bath visits, because it is 45 minutes of lying back in a 4-person salt room for €22
best_for.skip_html: if you want to explore anything; this is a built salt room for relaxation, not a natural cave or a tour

items.a: A man-made salt room, not a cave you explore. Highest price per hour here, about €29. Ages 14+ only, and not if you have a cold.
